From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Preflight: dependencies, exceptions, and doc ownership (release X.2)

Morning all — kicking off a short preflight thread for the X.2 release. We have a hard ETA to start customer rollouts on Monday 11/23 and I want to make sure we have clear owners for the open items below. Quick asks: please reply with status and owner if you are not the owner listed.

1) Documentation: final public runbook + per-customer checklist (owner: marcus) — are the changes from the safety/limits doc merged?
2) Exceptions: Acme asked for a short-term SLA exception around concurrency (see attached request) — need a decision and a can-we-deliver note (owner: laura).
3) Product asks: small API shape tweak (optional) to include route_id in response for routing telemetry — require engineering blessing/impact (owner: aditya).
4) Demo readiness: runbook + test account for Acme (owner: marcus) — can we guarantee a smoke window before Monday?

Attachments: preflight-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix of items), runbook-demo-checklist.pdf

If any of these need to be escalated, flag it in your reply and I'll escalate to ops/leadership.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kimberly — quick status from Docs/Enablement:
- Public runbook: draft updated with safety/limits changes (PR submitted). Waiting on a technical confirmation on the API shape change (Aditya). If we get the green light today I can merge and publish an interim runbook version.
- Per-customer checklist: templates ready. Need Acme-specific steps (demo creds + IP allowlist) from Laura before I finalize.
- Demo smoke: I can run a smoke window tomorrow (11/22) at 10:00 PT assuming the test account is provisioned.

Owner confirmations: Marcus (docs/runbook), will take runbook merge once engineering confirms.

Marcus Lin

Forwarding the procurement thread with Acme for context:

-----Original Message-----
From: Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Sent: Fri, Nov 20, 2026 16:40:02 -0500
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Subject: Re: SLA exception request for X.2 rollout

Hi Laura — Acme is asking for a temporary concurrency SLA bump: 200 -> 400 for the first 72 hours of their initial rollout. They said it's critical for their acceptance tests. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity-only exception (we can allocate) or requires code-path/backpressure changes?

Laura (release ops): we can provision burst capacity to Acme in Dedicated for three days but we need a written exception and an ops runbook for throttling fallback if we hit limits. I _think_ we can do this without infra changes but need to confirm with Eng.

Laura Bennett
Release Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preflight: dependencies, exceptions, and doc ownership (release X.2)

Short engineering read: the API shape tweak to add route_id in the response is backwards-compatible if we ship it as an opt-in header (Prefer: route-id). No infra changes required for the concurrency exception — we can provision short-term burst in Dedicated and configure the autoscaler to honor the higher target. Two notes:
- We'll need to run a load test against their expected patterns before enabling the burst; recommend the smoke window Marcus suggested.
- I'll push a small SR (INF-4821) to add the optional header and a config flag for the rollout. Target to merge by EOD today if no objections.

Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Thanks — good alignment. Quick summary and action items (please mark done in the sheet):
- Marcus: merge runbook (publish interim) once Aditya confirms the opt-in header is merged. Confirmed owner.
- Aditya: merge INF-4821 (opt-in route_id header) and run the load test against Acme pattern tomorrow AM. Confirmed owner and ETA: EOD today for PR, load test 11/22 09:00 PT.
- Laura: provision Dedicated burst capacity for Acme (72h) and prepare the throttling fallback runbook. Confirmed owner; please share the provisioning ticket/ops playbook link.
- Kimberly: I'll prepare the exception memo for legal/procurement and loop in Sales (cc'd after this thread).

If we hit any blockers by 18:00 PT I'll escalate to the SRE lead. Otherwise I'll close the preflight and send the go/no-go note by 20:00 PT.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround on a holiday weekend.

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager — Redwood Inference
